exchanges.sparringResponse:
Yes. Bad pattern, and here's the actual reasoning, not just the verdict: it exploits sunk cost instead of earning the conversion. The user already spent effort assuming a Soll-Zustand (finish the task) that the product quietly changes the rules on mid-stream. That's not persuading someone of value, that's trapping them with their own labor. In the Dortmund design-theory sense, that's a Rahmenbedingung the designer hid instead of declaring upfront, you're withholding the actual constraint of the system until the user has no good exit.
